memory.content: lead_time_days must always return a strictly positive value (>= 1), enforced by the final `days.max(1)` clamp applied AFTER the priority discount. Callers depend on this: promise_day (promise_board.rs) computes `today + lead_time_days(...) as u32`, so a 0 would promise same-day delivery and a negative i64 would wrap to a huge u32 when cast; the capacity hints in audit_log.rs, fleet_log.rs, and heartbeat.rs likewise cast the result `as usize`. The clamp must stay after the match so any future priority variant with a larger discount than Express's -2 (which can already drive short routes to 0) remains safe.
